So, you can't speak,

The first thing I always tell my students: you will never learn to speak and will not
speak fluently if you do not speak. This can be compared to a situation,
when a child who cannot walk yet learns to walk. He goes and falls,
but he gets up and keeps going, then falls again and then gets up again and
goes. This is the same as what happens when you learn a foreign language.
Many of you are afraid to speak because you make mistakes. So what? You keep
speaking! Nothing happened if you made a mistake. Nothing! Just keep speaking.
Also, many say they are afraid to talk because they forget words. But we have other
words. If you forget one word, you can say what you wanted to say differently.
See? All problems can be solved.
Now let's talk about what can be done
to help yourself speak better and more freely in Russian.
I always recommend my students read texts on different topics. For example,
if you want to learn to speak on the topic 'Sports'. You can take a text,
that suits your level – a text about sports, read this text,
try to understand it, remember new words and expressions for you. And it's important that later you can
discuss this text with your teacher, friend, or with yourself. And try to use
new words and expressions you encountered in this text during the discussion. The more you
use new words and expressions, the faster they will stick in your memory.
Of course, I recommend not only reading texts. You can listen to podcasts or watch videos on
some topic and do the same. I like to first give students a text so they have
a basic set of words related to some topic, and then I give students a podcast,
video, or maybe a more difficult text, where there are words we already know, but there are also
new words that expand our vocabulary on this topic. And, of course, we definitely discuss
everything we read, because this discussion simulates communication on this topic. Thus
over time (of course, not immediately) you will learn to speak on more and more topics.
I also want to draw your attention to the fact that there are many topics, that's true. We can talk about sports,
about ecology, about studying, about politics, and so on. If you are still at a not very high
level (you understand native speakers, but your grammar level may not be very high),
try to look in the textbook for the level you are at, the list of topics you
should be able to talk about at your level now. And try to work with these topics. Then,
when your grammar level becomes higher, so you can talk about more complex topics,
take a textbook for the next level and see what topics will be there.
If you can't find texts, that's also not a big problem, because now there are
a huge number of resources with texts on different topics. I wrote about this on my Instagram.
